messages.author: c6847fe2e1ee86d3
messages.subject: interpreting sex ratio
parts:
Hello,

How should I interpret the sex ratio (psi) for the following model results? 

mod.den.habitat.telm
 Model:  D ~ Habitat p0 ~ 1 sigma ~ 1
 Run time:  187.808  minutes
 AIC:  7313.429
 
Summary table: 
                Estimate    SE       z P(>|z|)
p0.(Intercept)    -7.155 0.385 -18.605   0.000
sig.(Intercept)    7.005 0.042 167.681   0.000
d0.(Intercept)    -3.429 0.367  -9.334   0.000
d.beta.Habitat2   -0.433 0.213  -2.029   0.042
d.beta.Habitat3    0.096 0.179   0.538   0.591
d.beta.Habitat4   -0.700 0.230  -3.044   0.002
psi.constant       0.505 0.151   3.337   0.001
*Density intercept is log(individuals per pixel) 
  Nhat(state-space) = exp(d0.)*nrow(ssDF)
  (caution is warranted when model contains density covariates)


Best,

David

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re:  [oscr] interpreting sex ratio
parts:
﻿That is the logit-scale probability of being a male, so inv.logit(0.505) = 0.62.
